title: Niteshift Raises $7M Seed to Build AI Coding Tools Without Big AI Lock-In
description: Datadog veterans launched AI coding startup Niteshift with a $7 million seed round led by Greylock's Jerry Chen. The startup is betting against big AI lock-in, positioning itself as an alternative in the competitive AI coding agent market alongside players like Cursor, Windsurf, and the major tech companies.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI Launches Lockdown Mode to Prevent Data Exfiltration
description: OpenAI rolled out Lockdown Mode for eligible accounts to help prevent the final stage of data exfiltration from prompt injection attacks by limiting outbound network requests. The feature directly attacks the 'exfiltration vectors' leg of the Lethal Trifecta (private data access + untrusted content exposure + data theft transmission). Simon Willison notes this implies ChatGPT's default settings don't provide robust protection against determined data exfiltration attacks.
author: Simon Willison

title: Charity Majors on AI Enthusiasts vs Skeptics: Both Racing Against Different Threats
description: Charity Majors captures the dynamic between AI enthusiasts and skeptics in software teams: enthusiasts are racing against time as discontinuous capability leaps create existential threats for teams that don't adopt AI, while skeptics race against entropy as shipping code faster than engineers can read it degrades reliability and evaporates institutional knowledge. The key issue: there's no natural feedback loop connecting the two groups.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Charity Majors)

title: Uber Caps AI Tool Usage at $1,500 Monthly Per Tool to Manage Costs
description: After blowing through its 2026 AI budget in four months, Uber is limiting employees to $1,500 in monthly token spending per AI coding tool. The limits apply specifically to agentic coding software like Cursor and Claude Code. This policy reveals Uber's valuation of AI tools at ~11% of median engineer compensation ($330,000/year), or ~$36,000 per engineer annually in AI spending. Simon Willison notes his own $1,000/month usage per provider would leave $500/month spare under Uber's caps.
author: Simon Willison

title: Microsoft Announces MAI-Thinking-1 (1T params, 35B active) and MAI-Code-1-Flash (137B params, 5B active)
description: Microsoft released two new text LLMs: MAI-Thinking-1, a 1T parameter reasoning model with 35B active parameters claimed preferred to Sonnet 4.6 in blind evaluations; and MAI-Code-1-Flash, a 137B parameter model with 5B active parameters purpose-built for GitHub Copilot and VS Code. Both are claimed to be trained on 'clean and appropriately licensed' data without distillation from third-party models. Simon Willison later corrected initial notes about model sizes and discovered the training data includes standard web crawls with similar licensing issues to other major LLMs.
author: Simon Willison
